title: crux refutation record (format_version 1)
description: Binds the named checks that settled a council round's blocking findings, and the result tokens those checks emitted, to seat-qualified finding ids so the gate check can read them. It applies to adr modules only. A conductor's record carries its round's reviewed subject hash; only an adjudicator's record, at an adr module's round 3, may check the subject as it stands. No vendored writer exists: the recorder names itself, so recorder identity is self-asserted.

written_at.$comment: UTC with microseconds, stamped by the recorder. The record takes its place in record order by this stamp, after the council record it names.

path.$comment: Repository-relative path of the council record this refutes.

sha256.$comment: sha256 of that council record's file bytes.

subjects.$comment: The subject hashes the checks ran against. A conductor's record must carry exactly the hashes its council record reviewed.

items.$comment: One entry per blocking finding. The result is derived from the token: result_token equal to expect is `refuted`; `verdict:INCONCLUSIVE` is `inconclusive`; any other token is `confirmed`. A recorded result that differs from the derived one refuses the record, and so do a missing token, an unknown finding id and a duplicate entry.

check.$comment: The command or named check that was run.

expect.$comment: The token the check emits when the finding is refuted.

result_token.$comment: An exit code, a pass count or a named verdict the check emitted; never a verdict word the recorder writes.

artifact.$comment: Repository-relative path of an in-repository artifact holding the check's output.
